subsystems.name: Engineered pigment cells
subsystems.role: produce and move pigments to change skin colour.

subsystems.name: Cue sensing and signalling
subsystems.role: detect mood or environmental signals and convert them into cellular commands.

subsystems.name: Dermal integration matrix
subsystems.role: anchors the engineered cells in skin and nourishes them.

subsystems.name: Control and programming interface
subsystems.role: lets the user set or read colour patterns.

subsystems.name: Safety and fail-safe system
subsystems.role: prevents uncontrolled pigment production or immune reaction.

buildSteps.title: Design genetic circuits
buildSteps.detail: Use synthetic biology to write DNA sequences that make a cell produce pigment only when a chosen signal is present.

buildSteps.title: Engineer cells
buildSteps.detail: Take human cells (e.g. induced pluripotent stem cells) and insert the circuits, then differentiate them into pigment-producing cells.

buildSteps.title: Test in culture
buildSteps.detail: Grow the cells in the lab, expose them to the trigger signals and measure the resulting colour change.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate or edit for immune acceptance
buildSteps.detail: Modify cells or coat them in a protective gel so the body's immune system does not attack them.

buildSteps.title: Deliver into skin
buildSteps.detail: Inject or graft the cells into the epidermis or dermis at the desired location.

buildSteps.title: Grow blood supply
buildSteps.detail: Stimulate the formation of tiny blood vessels to feed the cells with nutrients and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Connect sensing
buildSteps.detail: Link the cells to biological sensors (e.g. for cortisol) or external sensors that detect light, temperature or other environmental cues.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and program
buildSteps.detail: Map signal levels to specific colours and set up a user interface for control.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Regularly check cell health and replace them if needed, over months or years.

prerequisites.why: simple circuits work in bacteria and mammalian cells, but complex multi-input ones that respond to mood are still research.

prerequisites.tech: Cell therapy and skin tissue engineering
prerequisites.why: skin grafts are routine, but engineered pigment cells have not yet been used in humans.
light- and drug-controlled receptors are established research tools, though not yet in commercial human therapy.
the body usually rejects foreign cells; encapsulation or gene editing is not yet reliable for long-term skin integration.
we can measure some hormones and neural signals, but mapping them reliably to mood is not solved.

pathway.milestone: engineered human cells change colour on command in a dish
cells survive and function in animal skin for months
pathway.unlocks: understanding of integration and immune response.

pathway.milestone: safety and limited colour change in volunteers, likely for medical or cosmetic use
a commercial patch or treatment that offers limited colour options
pathway.unlocks: wider adoption and refinement of the technology.
new forms of visual communication and camouflage.
